skill.name: uv
skill.description: Use when managing Python projects with uv: fast virtualenvs, dependency resolution, lockfiles, and a pip-compatible interface from Astral.
whenToUse: Creating and managing Python virtual environments quickly
Installing and locking project dependencies via pyproject.toml
Replacing pip, pip-tools, and venv with one fast tool
Pinning and switching Python interpreter versions per project

keyConcepts.explanation: uv has a project workflow (uv add/sync/lock around pyproject.toml) and a low-level pip-compatible interface (uv pip install/compile) for existing workflows.
A universal, cross-platform lockfile uv generates and respects to make installs reproducible; managed automatically by uv sync/add.
uv can download and manage standalone CPython builds, so `uv python install 3.12` provisions interpreters without system Python.
Project commands create and use a .venv in the project root automatically; uv run executes inside it without manual activation.
Compiles requirements.in into a fully pinned requirements.txt, a drop-in faster pip-tools replacement.
uv hard-links/copies from a shared cache for fast, deduplicated installs across projects.

apiReference.purpose: Create a virtual environment, optionally pinning the interpreter version.
pip-compatible install into the active or project environment.
apiReference.example:
uv pip install 'requests>=2.31'
uv pip install -r requirements.txt

apiReference.signature: uv add / uv sync / uv lock
apiReference.purpose: Project workflow: add a dependency to pyproject.toml, sync the env to the lockfile, and regenerate the lock.
apiReference.example:
uv init myapp
cd myapp
uv add fastapi
uv sync

apiReference.purpose: Run a command inside the project environment, syncing first if needed.
apiReference.example:
uv run python main.py
uv run pytest

gotchas: `uv pip install` does not modify pyproject.toml or uv.lock; use `uv add` for project dependencies you want tracked.
uv pip operates on the active/discovered environment, not the global system Python, so activate or use --python deliberately.
uv sync prunes packages not in the lockfile by default, removing anything you installed manually with uv pip.
uv run auto-syncs the environment, so it may install/uninstall packages before running your command.
uv venv does not auto-activate; you still must source the activate script or rely on uv run.
Managed Python interpreters are separate from system Python; mixing them can cause confusing version mismatches.
